name: Modular figure assembly
summary: A figure is made in many standard parts, such as heads, torsos, arms and props, and the parts are joined and finished by hand. One set of moulds gives many different figures.
how: Model the figure and cut it into parts.
Press or cast each part in its own mould.
Join the parts with slip while the clay is soft.
Finish the joins and the face by hand, so that each figure differs.

origin.note: The state workshops of the First Emperor make heads and hands in moulds and join them to hand-built bodies.

adoptions.via: Workshops build the torso by coils, press the head in a two-piece mould and finish each face by hand.
Meissen modellers cast figures in many small piece moulds and join arms, heads and props with slip.
Vincennes and Sèvres cast biscuit figures in piece moulds, and cut the seams until they disappear.
